moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Lease income is contractually secured under lease agreements with reputed lessees, which management describes as stable and steady
- Licensed brand rights held by the UK subsidiary - FILA for specific distribution in the UK and Middle East, and Sergio Techcnini in the UK
- Very low fixed-cost base: only 8 employees on the rolls as at 31st March 2026
- Internal audit carried out by an external firm of Chartered Accountants; management considers the present control system adequate for the current business

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- MD&A states the disturbance in West Asia is expected to impact trading activity due to challenging logistic issues and that the West Asia war is expected to impact revenue in the medium term; management keeps the external situation under watch.
- Management explicitly says trading AND lease income may both be affected to a certain extent by the West Asia war - the company has only these two income lines, so there is no third stream to absorb the hit.
- The operating profit margin ratio stayed flat year on year, which management attributes to tight margins on the trading business - revenue growth of around 48% did not translate into margin expansion.
- Under Opportunity and Threats, management states that although it will keep exploring opportunities where it has expertise, considering the geopolitical situation the opportunities are very limited - constraining growth beyond the existing two activities.
- BB (UK) Ltd. consolidated revenue from operations fell year on year and a similar trend is expected to continue due to adverse market conditions; the Board notes the brands face intense competition in BB (UK)'s territories and worldwide, with geopolitical disturbance expected to disrupt the market further in the medium term.
- The Directors' Report attributes marginally lower other income to lower dividends received from the overseas subsidiary BB (UK) Ltd., so group other income moves with the UK subsidiary's ability to distribute.
- BB (UK) Ltd. operates on licences - FILA for specific distribution in the UK and Middle East and Sergio Techcnini in the UK - rather than owned brands, per the Directors' Report.
- Income from lease is described as contractually secured under lease agreements with reputed lessees and steady in line with the current market trend; it is therefore tied to the renewal and continuation of those specific contracts.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue to explore any new business opportunity where the company has expertise, while acknowledging that opportunities are very limited given the geopolitical situation
- Sustain the textile trading business, whose turnover grew around 48% during the year and where management expects the growth momentum to continue
- Keep lease income contractually secured through lease agreements with reputed lessees
- Keep the external situation under watch, reviewed by top management and supported by the internal audit process carried out by an external firm of Chartered Accountants
